title: The Fake Prom
premise: August Reyes has spent years keeping her family afloat and invisible, so when she finds coded instructions hidden in her late grandmother's recipe box—directions for uncovering the school board's buried scandal—she wants to burn them. But the secret ties to her grandmother's own disappearance from the district decades ago, and to money quietly siphoned from the very programs keeping kids like August fed. As prom approaches, August and her best friend Priya decode the trail while the board's youngest member, Ms. Calloway, watches them with unsettling interest. At prom itself, August triggers the exposure in front of the whole school, forcing a resignation and an apology that is too small but still hers—and choosing, finally, to be seen.
about_author: Mara Vane grew up in a rust-belt town where school levies failed more often than they passed, and she never stopped noticing who paid for it. She writes stories about teenagers holding up more than anyone should ask of them.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: August's POV. A chaotic morning: burnt toast, missing bus fare, little brother Mateo's field trip fee she can't cover. She lies smoothly to a teacher about 'mom handling it.' Establishes her competence and exhaustion; emotional beat of proud, practiced denial.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: August's POV. Cleaning out grandma's closet, she finds the tin recipe box—inside, cards written like recipes but describing people, dates, and amounts. 'Fold in the levy funds. Serves twelve, secretly.' Beat: curiosity overriding fear.

chapters.title: Serves Twelve
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The friends decode three cards at the diner; Priya recognizes the names as former school board members. First card references 'the Harvest Fund,' which no longer exists. Beat: thrill curdling into unease when August realizes grandma wrote these.

chapters.title: Mom Works Nights
chapters.summary: August's POV. Mom comes home at dawn; August almost tells her, then sees how hollowed out she is and swallows it. A quiet scene of reversed parent-child roles. Beat: loneliness inside responsibility.

chapters.title: The Empty Auditorium
chapters.summary: August's POV. She sneaks into school after hours following card four's clues to a sealed storage room behind the auditorium. Finds old boxes labeled HARVEST FUND 1998. Someone else is already there—or was; a dropped lanyard reads CALLOWAY. Beat: dread.

chapters.title: Ms. Calloway, Nicely
chapters.summary: August's POV. The young board member invites August to 'talk college' and asks oddly specific questions about her grandmother. August plays dumb, heart hammering. Beat: the first sense of being hunted instead of hidden.

chapters.title: Mateo Knows Something
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV (brief). Little brother mentions a teacher told his class the Harvest Fund pays for their field trips—which contradicts everything. August realizes the theft is ongoing, not historical. Beat: protective fury ignites purpose.

chapters.title: Cards Five Through Nine
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Decoding montage: the cards trace money through a shell charity called Bright Table. Priya builds a spreadsheet; August resists going public because 'nobody believes kids.' Beat: partnership deepens, stakes clarify.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: August's POV. Dragged onto prom committee by circumstance, she discovers the dance is funded by Bright Table—a PR laundering scheme. Calloway chairs the committee, smiling too much. Beat: the enemy is everywhere, wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Grandma's Last Card
chapters.summary: August's POV. A final card, different handwriting pressure, dated two weeks before grandma died: 'If you're reading this, mija, they'll come smiling. Don't sign anything.' Flashback fragments of grandma's warnings. Beat: grief becomes inheritance.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: August's POV. Calloway offers August a full-ride scholarship 'through Bright Table' if she returns some 'family papers.' The corruption literally prices her future. Beat: temptation—the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: Refusal, Privately Terrifying
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. August tells Priya she refused; they realize refusing means Calloway may retaliate against mom's job at the district. Stakes go home. They plan to move fast before prom. Beat: fear converted to resolve.

chapters.title: Following the Money Home
chapters.summary: August's POV. County records office scene: Bright Table's director is the current board president, Mr. Hask. Grandma's cards name him directly. August photographs everything with shaking hands. Beat: the villain has a name and a handshake.

chapters.title: The Leak That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. They approach a local reporter, who seems interested—then a story runs early, garbled, discrediting 'conspiracy-minded students.' They've been played or bugged. Beat: betrayal and setback; trust fractures between the girls briefly.

chapters.title: Mom Finds Out
chapters.summary: August's POV. Mom finds the recipe box open on the kitchen table. Instead of forbidding her, mom reveals grandma was fired in '98 for asking about the fund. Three generations, one silence. Beat: family solidarity replaces protection-by-secrecy.

chapters.title: Prom Dress, War Plans
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A lighter chapter: dress shopping with donated coupons, laughing until it hurts, then mapping the prom-night plan—AV booth, slideshow swap, press invited anonymously. Beat: joy as fuel; found-family warmth before the storm.

chapters.title: Calloway's Confession
chapters.summary: August's POV. Calloway corners August, drops the mask partially: she took the job to fix it from inside and got swallowed. She gives August one true piece of evidence—then warns prom will be watched. Beat: ambiguous ally; moral complexity.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: August's POV. Quiet domestic scene: ironing a borrowed dress, Mateo asleep, mom leaving for her shift with 'Make them look at you.' August rereads grandma's last card. Beat: stillness, terror, love.

chapters.title: The Fake Prom
chapters.summary: August's POV. Prom begins glittering and hollow; Bright Table banners everywhere. August and Priya execute the AV swap—but the file is blocked remotely. Hask takes the stage to toast himself. Beat: trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Look At Me
chapters.summary: August's POV. Improvising, August grabs the mic during the toast and speaks—not reading evidence, just telling the truth about hungry kids and stolen funds while Calloway, honoring her word, unlocks the AV feed live. The real slideshow plays. Beat: climax; visibility as victory.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unresolved
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Hask resigns under investigation; the scholarship offer evaporates; a fundraiser restores partial funding. Justice is real but incomplete. August feels lighter and angrier than expected. Beat: the price of survival acknowledged, not erased.

chapters.title: Recipe for Starting Over
chapters.summary: August's POV. Epilogue in June: mom days, Mateo's trip paid by restored funds, grandma's box on the shelf—now mixed with August's own new cards, the first reading like a recipe for courage. Final beat: staying visible, on purpose.
